headline: Personal Money & Banking · Spanish · Foundation
threshold: Use Spanish to complete the foundation personal money & banking conversations and explain the next step.

lessons.title: Name everyday money amounts
lessons.objective: Read a shop total aloud, name the banknotes and coins used to pay, and ask for the change and receipt in Spanish.
lessons.focus: Dollar amounts with the $ sign; cuesta and cuestan agreement; the verb costar

words.note: Paper money. Un billete de veinte dólares is a twenty-dollar bill.
Metal money. Use monedas for coins in the plural.
The full amount to pay after all items are added.
The money returned when you pay with more than the price.
In a shop, cajero or cajera is the person who takes payment. At a bank, the word means ATM.
One hundredth of a dollar. Fifty cents is written $0.50.
Banknotes and coins, not a card payment.

words.en: Could you give me the change, please?
Could you give me the receipt, please?

lessons.speaking: You are buying bread and milk at a small shop counter. Ask the price of the milk, pay with a twenty-dollar bill, and ask for the change and the receipt. Finish by repeating the total and the change aloud so the cashier can confirm them.

lessons.title: Ask about a bank account
lessons.objective: Ask what a checking or savings account is for, ask which documents to bring, and check the minimum balance before opening.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, para qué and cuál; the verbs abrir, necesitar and servir

words.note: Used for daily payments. In Mexico many people say cuenta de cheques.
Cuenta de ahorros means savings account.
An official photo ID such as a passport or driver license.
A physical bank office where clients meet staff.
The lowest amount the account must keep.
A recent bill or statement that shows your home address.

words.en: What documents do I need to bring?

words.es: Quiero abrir una cuenta de ahorros.
words.en: I want to open a savings account.
Is there a minimum balance to open it?

words.note: Hoy mismo stresses this very day.

lessons.speaking: You visit a bank branch to open an account. Ask what the checking account is for, ask which documents you must bring, and ask whether there is a minimum balance. Close by confirming the single document you will bring next time and thanking the staff member.
lessons.partnerRole: Spanish-speaking bank adviser at a branch desk
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar hoy?

lessons.title: Read your balance
lessons.objective: Tell the current balance from the available balance and explain why a pending purchase may change the available amount.
lessons.focus: Present tense of aparecer and incluir; singular and plural agreement with the thing that appears

words.note: The balance after posted transactions.
The amount you can spend now, after holds are subtracted.
Authorized but not yet final. Esa compra está pendiente means the purchase is not final.
A temporary block on money. It is not yet a charge.
One line of money in or out in the account history.
In Spain the same document is called extracto.
The quantity of money in a transaction; common across Latin America.

words.en: When does it show up in my balance?

words.es: El saldo actual incluye todos los cargos.
words.en: The current balance includes all the charges.

lessons.speaking: You are checking a banking app at a bus stop because you need to pay rent. Ask the bank helper for your available balance, ask why it is lower than the current balance, and ask when the pending purchase will appear. Close by stating the amount you can safely spend today.
lessons.partnerRole: Spanish-speaking bank support assistant on a phone line
lessons.openingLine: Hola, soy Diego del servicio al cliente. ¿Me dice su número de cuenta?

lessons.title: Make a deposit
lessons.objective: State the amount of a cash and check deposit, confirm the total, and ask when the funds become available.
lessons.focus: Estar for location and availability; the future estará for scheduled availability

words.note: The counter where clients do transactions with a teller in person.
A bank teller at the counter, feminine form.
Proof of a completed deposit or payment, printed or digital. The form filled in before a deposit is often called ficha de depósito.
A written order to pay money from a bank account. Cheque de viajero means traveler check.

words.en: I want to make a deposit of $150.00.

words.es: ¿Me puede confirmar el monto, por favor?
words.en: Could you confirm the amount for me, please?
The funds will be available tomorrow.

words.es: Aquí está el comprobante de depósito.

lessons.speaking: You are at a teller window with cash and a check. State that you want to deposit $150.00, confirm the amount, and ask when the money will be available. Close by repeating the availability date and taking the deposit slip.
lessons.partnerRole: Spanish-speaking bank teller at a counter window
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar hoy?

lessons.title: Withdraw cash
lessons.objective: Request an amount at the window, ask for the bill sizes you want, and count the cash before leaving.
lessons.focus: Polite requests with puede and the verb form for usted; contar and entregar

words.note: A cash withdrawal from an account. Retiro de efectivo is the full phrase.
Cajero automático is used across Latin America. Spain often says cajero.
The value of each bill or coin, such as twenty dollars.
A queue of people waiting. Hacer fila means to wait in line.

words.es: Quiero retirar $200.00 en efectivo, por favor.
words.en: I want to withdraw $200.00 in cash, please.

words.es: ¿Puede darme billetes de veinte, por favor?
words.en: Can you give me twenty-dollar bills, please?

words.es: ¿Cuál es mi límite diario de retiro?
words.en: What is my daily withdrawal limit?

words.es: Cuento el efectivo antes de salir.
words.en: I count the cash before leaving.

lessons.speaking: You need cash for a plumber, so you go to the bank window. Ask for $200.00 in cash, ask for twenty-dollar bills and some smaller bills, and ask what your daily limit is. Close by counting the cash aloud and confirming the amount with the teller.
lessons.partnerRole: Spanish-speaking bank teller at a cash window
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Qué tipo de operación quiere hacer hoy?

lessons.title: Use a debit or credit card
lessons.objective: Ask which cards a shop accepts, say which account a purchase affects, and explain the difference between paying from your balance and paying with credit.
lessons.focus: Este and esta with a noun, and the verb afectar with a direct object

words.note: Money leaves your bank account when the payment is processed.
Creates a bill you pay later; the balance is owed to the card issuer.
The machine that reads a card or phone at the till.
A shop or business that accepts card payments.
The monthly document for a credit card that shows the balance owed and the payment due date. Factura is a merchant invoice.
On a bill, fecha de vencimiento is the payment due date. Printed on a card, it is the expiry date. Fecha límite de pago is unambiguous.

words.es: Pase la tarjeta por la terminal.
words.en: Run the card through the terminal.
Does this payment affect my account?

lessons.speaking: You are at a pharmacy counter with a card. Ask whether the shop accepts debit cards, ask whether the payment will affect your checking account or your credit limit, and ask if you can pay contactless. Close by saying which card you chose and why.
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Tiene todo lo que necesita o le busco algo más?

lessons.title: Find a transaction in an app
lessons.objective: Locate the amount, date, merchant and payment status of one purchase on a banking app screen.
lessons.focus: Imperative with usted for on-screen instructions; the verbs buscar, escribir and cambiar

words.note: The list of past activity in an app.
Estado del pago means payment status.
Money returned to you after a purchase is reversed or corrected.
Captura de pantalla means screenshot.

words.es: Me llegó una notificación del banco.
words.en: I received a notification from the bank.

words.es: Escriba el nombre del comercio en el buscador.
words.en: Type the merchant name in the search box.

words.es: Use el filtro de fecha, por favor.

lessons.speaking: Your father is helping you find a store charge on a banking app. Describe the purchase you remember, ask him to search for the store and the date, and read the amount and payment status aloud. Close by saying whether you will ask the bank about a refund.
lessons.partnerRole: Spanish-speaking father helping with a phone app
lessons.openingLine: Hija, ¿qué compra quieres encontrar en la aplicación?

lessons.title: Identify income and spending
lessons.objective: Describe money that comes in, separate fixed costs from variable spending, and name one amount set aside for saving.
lessons.focus: Subject-verb agreement with plural amounts and the verbs trabajar, sumar and separar

words.note: Money paid out. Gasto fijo and gasto variable are the two main groups.
Regular pay for work, often per month or per pay period.
Paid twice a month, often on the 15th and the last day. Pay every two weeks is cada dos semanas.
Money paid to rent a home. In Spain the usual word is alquiler.
A regular bill for electricity, water, internet or phone service.

words.es: Mi ingreso llega cada quince días.
words.en: My income arrives every fifteen days.

words.es: Pago la renta el primero de cada mes.
words.en: I pay the rent on the first day of each month.
How much do I spend each month on food?
The fixed costs add up to $644.99.

words.es: Separo un ahorro antes de gastar.
words.en: I set aside savings before I spend.

lessons.speaking: Describe your money in a simple way: say how often your income arrives, name two fixed costs with amounts, and say what you spend on food each month. Close by naming one amount you will set aside before you spend, and ask the tutor whether that amount is realistic.
lessons.partnerRole: Spanish-speaking money tutor at a community center
lessons.openingLine: Hola. Cuénteme qué dinero entra y qué dinero sale cada mes.

lessons.title: Set a simple savings goal
lessons.objective: State what you are saving for, the total amount, the monthly contribution and the target date.
lessons.focus: Infinitive after a verb of wanting (quiero ahorrar) and the present tense for routine actions

words.note: Money kept for unexpected costs, separate from a trip or a purchase goal.

words.en: I want to save $1,200.00 for a trip.
How much should I contribute each month?

words.es: Pongo una transferencia automática cada quincena.
words.en: I set up an automatic transfer twice a month.

words.es: Esa meta es realista con mi presupuesto.
words.en: That goal is realistic with my budget.

words.es: ¿En qué fecha puedo alcanzar la meta?
words.en: On what date can I reach the goal?

lessons.speaking: Set a goal for a trip. State the amount and the purpose, say how long you have, and ask the adviser how much to contribute each month. Close by stating your monthly contribution and the date you aim to reach it.
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué meta de ahorro quiere empezar?

lessons.title: Ask for help clearly
lessons.objective: Explain one money question, ask for a slower explanation, request a written summary and confirm the next step.
lessons.focus: Polite requests with puede plus infinitive and attached pronouns (explicármelo); the verbs explicar, repetir and enviar

words.note: A specific charge for a service, such as a low-balance fee.
The code the bank gives you so the call or case can be found.

words.en: Could you explain it to me more slowly?

words.es: ¿Me puede repetir el número de referencia?
words.en: Could you repeat the reference number for me?

words.es: Entonces confirmo que mañana reviso el cargo.
words.en: So I confirm that tomorrow I will check the charge.
Can you send me a summary in writing?

lessons.speaking: Call customer service about a fee you do not understand. Ask a clear question, ask the agent to explain more slowly, ask for the next step in writing, and repeat the reference number. Close by confirming what you will check tomorrow.
lessons.partnerRole: Spanish-speaking customer service agent on a phone line
lessons.openingLine: Atención al cliente, buenas tardes. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?
